why: jobId (validated as a UUID by the tool schema) is only used as a key into PipelineManager's in-memory jobMap to look up/cancel a job; it never reaches a path, command, SQL string, or eval.

sink: outbound HTTP(S) request to the caller-supplied URL's hostname (axios.get in HttpFetcher; Chromium's own network stack in BrowserFetcher's Playwright fallback)
guard: bypassable: ScraperAccessPolicy.assertNetworkUrlAllowed (src/utils/accessPolicy.ts:83-151) blocks private/special-use IPs, but it does this by resolving the hostname once via dns.promises.lookup at check time (accessPolicy.ts:83-151, called at HttpFetcher.ts:113 before the request); axios.get (line 161) then performs its own independent DNS resolution to actually connect, and nothing pins the checked address for that connection. An attacker who controls the authoritative DNS for the target hostname can answer the pre-check lookup with a public IP and the connect-time lookup, moments later, with a private/link-local address (e.g. 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254), defeating the check. The same applies to redirects: the Location header is revalidated (line 197) but the eventual connect to it is again a separate resolution.
why: url is directly caller-controlled per the tool's own zod schema (z.string().url()); it flows straight through AutoDetectFetcher into HttpFetcher, whose only SSRF defense is a check-then-connect hostname validation with no IP pinning between the two independent DNS resolutions. BrowserFetcher has the identical pattern (assertNetworkUrlAllowed before navigation, then Chromium resolves and connects on its own).
contract: Fetch a single URL and convert its content to Markdown. Use this tool to read the content of any web page.

why: library/targetVersion only feed a small bounded regex (/^(\d+)(?:\.(?:x(?:\.x)?|\d+(?:\.(?:x|\d+))?))?$|^$/, no nested quantifiers) and semver 7.8.5 (ReDoS fixes landed in 7.5.2) plus parameterized store lookups; no path/command/SQL sink is reached.
jobId is only used as a Map key in PipelineManager.getJob; it never reaches a path, command, SQL string, or eval.
status is a zod-validated enum used only to filter an in-memory job list; no caller-controlled string ever reaches a sink.
The tool takes no parameters at all (empty schema), so there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

library/version only feed the same bounded semver-coercion regex used by find_version (semver 7.8.5, ReDoS-patched) and parameterized store lookups; the eventual re-fetch reuses the version's already-stored, previously-validated sourceUrl rather than a fresh caller-supplied URL, so no new attacker-controlled string reaches the network/file sinks in this call.

library/version are only used in parameterized DocumentStore delete statements (db.prepare(...).run with ? placeholders) and an in-memory job-list filter by equality; no string concatenation into SQL/paths/commands occurs.

sink: new RegExp(userPattern) compiled from a caller-supplied string, then .test() run once per discovered URL/pathname/basename for every page visited during the crawl (src/scraper/strategies/BaseScraperStrategy.ts:144 shouldIncludeUrl -> patternMatcher.ts matchesAnyPattern/patternToRegExp)
why: The tool's own schema documents that '/pattern/' is treated as a literal regex the caller supplies, and PipelineManager.normalizeScraperOptions spreads options unchanged so includePatterns/excludePatterns reach patternToRegExp verbatim with no length/complexity limit or timeout. Because scrape_docs's url argument is also caller-controlled, an attacker can point it at their own site and pick both a catastrophic-backtracking pattern and page content/links engineered to hit it, hanging the scrape (and the shared worker) for the whole crawl (up to maxPages). Note: scrape_docs's url also goes through the same DNS-rebinding-bypassable SSRF check documented under fetch_url; that finding applies here too but only one row is filed per tool.
contract: Patterns for including/excluding URLs during scraping... Regex patterns must be wrapped in slashes, e.g. /pattern/.

why: DocumentStore.escapeFtsQuery (DocumentStore.ts:882) tokenizes the caller-supplied query with a quote-toggle state machine and doubles every embedded quote before building the FTS5 MATCH string, and library/version resolve through parameterized statements, preventing FTS5 query-syntax injection.
